text: The massive five-arm intersection of Bathurst, Lake Shore, and Fleet doesn't work well for anyone. It is a danger and a barrier for pedestrians, it is confusing for drivers and has a high rate of vehicle collisions, and it delays two streetcar lines. This intersection should tie together the three adjacent neighbourhoods – Bathurst Quay, Fort York, and CityPlace – but instead it separates them from one another. Going back to at least as far as 2004, before the Fort York and CityPlace neighbourhoods were constructed, the City of Toronto has made plans for reconfiguring this intersection. Concern about this intersection was one of the most common themes I heard from community members throughout the consultations for the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Plan in 2014 and 2015. City Council on October 29 and 30, 2019, adopted the following: 1. City Council rescind the westerly southbound right-turn only lane designation in effect at all times on Bathurst Street, between Lake Shore Boulevard West and a point 30.5 metres north. 2. City Council prohibit southbound right-turn movements at all times, Toronto Transit Commission vehicles excepted, on Bathurst Street at Lake Shore Boulevard West. 3. City Council designate the centre southbound through-lane on Bathurst Street, between Fleet Street and a point 40 metres north, for public transit vehicles only. 4. City Council direct the General Manager, Transportation Services to prioritize and expedite the implementation of these safety improvements, given the documented safety concern and collision history at this location. 5.
